contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside: 1 bracket and histogram reset, 1 in the count scan, 1 after the compaction stores, 3 per finishing pass (histogram, scan internal, state), 1 before the warp finish; the multi-pass emission adds 1 in its scan, the lazy tie test 1
contract.k_range: [1, N) at run time, the bound is accepted only when the candidate count is at least k (always for k <= Threads), else the tile fallback runs
contract.n_range: N = Threads x IPT, Threads 128, 256 or 512, IPT >= 1, N <= 32768 (16-bit count fields), measured 1024 to 32768 at 256 threads
contract.type_constraints: fp32 and bf16 keys, int32 indices derived from the striped position
contract.nan_behavior: the sweeps compare fp32 values (a NaN key is never a candidate and never a thread maximum unless all its items are NaN), the candidates are twiddled: a NaN with the sign bit clear orders above +inf, one with the sign bit set below -inf, the all-ones pattern collides with the empty-slot sentinel of the warp finish (unsupported), never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 equals +0.0 in the value-domain sweeps and is folded onto +0.0 when the candidates are twiddled under prefer_smaller_index
contract.tie_break_support: not_guaranteed and prefer_smaller_index, one code path: the warp finish orders the pivot set by (key descending, index ascending), a tie class larger than 32 is taken in ticket order under not_guaranteed and ranked by index passes under prefer_smaller_index, the items above the pivot set are an exact set under both
contract.sorted_output_support: not supported inherently, post-sort of k

correctness.notes: All 92 cells passed the oracle battery (13 cases per cell) under both requirements, including signed_zero under prefer_smaller_index (value-domain sweeps treat the zeros as equal, the fold happens at candidate load), tie_heavy, pivot_tie and all_equal (tile fallback), inf_denorm, sorted inputs.

low_level: Harness version: this card's cells were measured with harness 0.4, whose generate-only control launched without the variant's dynamic shared memory. Since harness 0.6 the control launches with it (dyn_floor), which raises the no-op slope of a control with a large shared buffer (B3_tuned: 10760 instead of 8676 cycles at fp32 N 32768 k 256, raw slope unchanged) and lowers its net latency at fp32 N 16384 and 32768 by 9 to 11 percent and at bf16 N 32768 k 256 by 4 to 5 percent. The B4_v4 values are unaffected except bf16 N 4096 (7 to 9 percent lower under 0.8, the no-op slope of the striped loads at IPT 16 is 654 instead of 254 cycles per call; the same source built with harness 0.4 on the verifier's node reproduces this card to 0.1 percent).

Changes against B4_v3: the pass histogram and the single-pass emission tickets are branch-free, every slot issues its shared atomic, to the bin when the slot takes part and to a private dummy word of the thread otherwise (T32's proposal), so no reconvergence region sits between the slots; the candidate loads are guarded per uniform group of four slots instead of loading all smax slots. Registers 64 at IPT 4, 126 to 128 at IPT 16 and 32, 255 from IPT 64, spill 2632 bytes (bf16) and 3416 (fp32) at IPT 128 against v3's 1648 and 1416 (the dummy-address selects keep 16 more addresses live), prefer_smaller_index 2560 and 2968.

Phase profile (clock64 stamps, median cycles): fp32 N 32768 k 256 bracket 454, count and scan 2438, compaction 1876, loads 730, pass 720 (v3 989), emission 2059 (v3 1792), total 8855 (v3 8904); bf16 N 4096 k 16 loads 682 (976), pass 742 (920), emission 1279 (1108), total 4221 (4452). The branch-free pass saves 200 to 270 cycles, the branch-free emission costs 170 to 270 more: sixteen atomicAdd with return per thread (ten of them to dummy words) and sixteen dependent bin-prefix loads cost more than six tickets behind branches, the atomic with return is 55 cycles and the shared atomic unit serves the whole block.

SASS: the pass body is SEL (address), SHF, LOP3, IADD, ATOMS per slot without BSSY, the emission body SEL, ATOMS (with return), LDS, IADD, two predicated STS per slot without BSSY. The group guards remain uniform branches per four slots.

Throughput (Gelem per s): N 32768 832 and 941 against 400 and 345 (2.08x and 2.73x), N 16384 669 and 738 against 465 and 312 (1.44x and 2.37x), N 8192 646 and 693 against 459 and 398 (1.41x and 1.74x), N 4096 414 and 417 against 543 and 459 (0.76x and 0.91x). Registers 255 from IPT 64 (B3_tuned 128 to 255), occupancy 1 block per SM at IPT 64 and 128 (B3_tuned 2 and 1).
negative: Branch-free atomics with return to dummy addresses (the emission tickets) do not pay: issuing an atomic with return for every slot costs more than the reconvergence regions it removes, because the returned value is on the critical path of the store and the extra atomics load the shared memory unit of the whole block. The same trick on fire-and-forget histogram atomics (the pass) pays about 200 cycles.
Neither v3 nor v4 moves the register sweeps (4700 cycles at IPT 128, half of the call); the instruction count per item is the lever and this session did not get to the packed bf16 arrangement.
surprises: T32's dummy-word proposal splits by atomic kind: a gain for fire-and-forget histogram increments, a loss for tickets with return.

After four builds the finish (loads, pass, emission, warp finish) is about 3300 cycles at every N and the sweeps scale with IPT at about 37 cycles per item: B4's cost is 3300 plus 37 x IPT, so it crosses B1_idx and B3_tuned between N 4096 and N 8192 and reaches 3x at N 32768.
open_questions: The emission tickets behind branches (v3) with the branch-free pass (v4) would combine the two gains, one more build.
Packed bf16 sweeps (T18, packed_striped arrangement) and a lighter block scan are the remaining levers for the sweeps and the structure, predicted 1000 and 300 cycles at N 32768.
A same-session pairing of the final variant with B1_idx and B2_twolevel (k 16) was not run within the batch budget, the chain through the B4_base cards stands in for it.

 Re-check 2026-10-25 after the amendment (swarm commits 891ec6fce9 and 3e09890223, B4 report section 10): the findings now state harness 0.4 and quote the 0.8 ratios, every quoted number matches the verify-B4 batches, the verification block is intact and the card validates. The cell values are unchanged (fp32 N 32768 k 256 6969 against 20021). The lead then ruled that pre-0.6 cards are judged under their own harness version with the 0.8 ratios recorded, so the flag is set to verified. Under that policy the B3_tuned fp32 N 32768 control was not reproduced under a 0.4 build (only the bf16 N 4096 cells were), waived by the lead because the final evaluation re-measures every winner under one harness and one session. Root cause confirmed by eval-engineer on 2026-10-25 (harness README section 3.1): under harness 0.2 to 0.9 the 16 harness inputs could be L1 resident, so the generate-only control's per-call load cost depended on the chain length (per-repetition working set) and on the L1 carve-out (the variant's shared memory through dyn_floor), and the min over repetitions picked cached repetitions for short chains. Harness 0.10 streams every harness load past L1 and gives each chain length a fixed strided subset of the inputs, under which B4_v4 bf16 N 4096 k 16 reads 3808 cycles, this card's value, and large-smem controls stay at the dyn_floor level.
